requirements.text: We are seeking a senior full-stack engineer with deep backend roots to build the next generation of application interfaces for an agent-driven world. Traditional UIs rely on static, step-by-step human workflows; our future surfaces rely on AI agents doing the bulk of the work while high-density dashboards give humans real-time visibility, intent control, and governance. To build interfaces that make complex, non-deterministic system state effortlessly clear, you must be someone who can write production agentic/AI code, reason deeply about distributed data architecture, and translate underlying backend complexity into intuitive, high-trust human experiences.

Traditional UIs rely on static, step-by-step human workflows; our future surfaces rely on AI agents doing the bulk of the work while high-density dashboards give humans real-time visibility, intent control, and governance. To build interfaces that make complex, non-deterministic system state effortlessly clear, you must be someone who can write production agentic/AI code, reason deeply about distributed data architecture, and translate underlying backend complexity into intuitive, high-trust human experiences.

Agentic Integration & Backend Execution: Design asynchronous workflows, event streams, and LLM/agent integration layers (tool-use, state machines, contextual memory) while ensuring resilience, auditability, and clear data provenance.

Innate Instincts for UI/UX & Information Design: A deep passion for human-computer interaction, data visualization, and micro-interactions. You care about friction vs. fluidity—knowing exactly when to require human intervention and how to clearly show causality and uncertainty.
Product & Platform Thinking: Ability to reason through multi-agent governance, context delegation, and high-trust developer/operator tools.
Experience building developer tools, observability platforms, complex control planes, or investigative analytics software.
A background or strong self-directed grounding in HCI (Human-Computer Interaction), design systems, or data visualization theory (e.g., Edward Tufte, Bret Victor, Tamara Munzner).
Track record of building zero-to-one developer platforms or open-source tooling for AI agent supervision.
